content.user_title: Manage Document IDs in Git Repositories
content.value_statement: Large repositories can lose track of document identity, references, and content changes. Shirushi helps validate, assign, scan, and rehash doc_ids across Markdown and YAML files.
actual_capabilities: Validate doc_ids and index integrity with shirushi lint.
List documents and metadata with shirushi scan.
Look up a document by doc_id with shirushi show.
Assign doc_ids to new Markdown or YAML documents.
Recalculate content hashes after document changes.
Explain Shirushi configuration for ID formats and dimensions.
limitations: Requires the Shirushi CLI to be installed in the working environment.
Works only with repositories that use Shirushi configuration and doc_id conventions.
Does not create the Shirushi CLI or replace its validation logic.
Command results depend on the current Git state and local files.

use_cases.title: Validate Documentation Before Commit
use_cases.description: Check doc_ids, indexes, and references before documentation changes enter source control.

use_cases.title: Find Document Metadata Quickly
use_cases.description: Use a doc_id to locate a document and review its registered metadata.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Request Reference Risk
use_cases.description: Compare documentation changes against the target branch and identify changed referenced documents.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Repository Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Shirushi to check this repository for doc_id and index integrity. Explain any issues and suggest fixes before commit.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Document by ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Find document <doc_id> with Shirushi, summarize its metadata, and tell me whether references appear current.

prompt_templates.title: Assign IDs to New Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Review new documentation files, assign missing Shirushi doc_ids where appropriate, and report the files changed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit PR Reference Integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Shirushi validation against the target branch, check @see docid references, and summarize risks for reviewers.

output_examples.input: Check document ID health before my documentation commit.
output_examples.output: The repository passed doc_id validation. Two references point to changed documents, so review those linked specifications before merging.
Shirushi found the document and returned its title, type, and file location. The ID is already registered in the index.

output_examples.input: Assign IDs to new documentation files.
output_examples.output: New document IDs were assigned to the untracked documentation files. The report lists each file and the generated ID.

best_practices: Run validation before committing documentation changes.
Keep Shirushi configuration aligned with your document taxonomy.
Review changed document references during pull requests.
anti_patterns: Do not edit existing doc_ids without a migration plan.
Do not run assignment on generated or temporary documents.
Do not ignore warnings about changed referenced documents.

faq.question: What does Shirushi manage?
faq.answer: It manages immutable doc_ids for Markdown and YAML documents in Git repositories.

faq.question: Does this skill install Shirushi?
faq.answer: No. The Shirushi CLI must already be available in the working environment.

faq.question: Can it assign IDs to new documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide use of Shirushi to assign missing doc_ids to new documentation files.

faq.question: Can it validate references?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check @see docid references when the repository and CLI support that workflow.

faq.question: Does it work outside Git repositories?
faq.answer: It is designed for Git repositories and uses Git context for common validation workflows.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
